title: Claude Code worktree ".git" naming -- T1546.004 sandbox-escaping shell config overwrite
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-55607 (GHSA-7835-87q9-rgvv,
CVSS 7.7 HIGH), a self-reported advisory for Claude Code (versions
`>= 2.1.38, < 2.1.163`), fixed in 2.1.163.

Claude Code's worktree handling allowed creating a git worktree literally
named `.git` and navigating to worktrees outside the sandbox context --
"git directory confusion". Combined with symlink manipulation and git
fsmonitor execution during worktree operations, this let an attacker
overwrite files in the user's home directory (the advisory names
`.zshenv` as the example), achieving code execution outside the macOS
seatbelt sandbox's restrictions the next time a shell starts. The
advisory is explicit that reliable exploitation required the user to
clone a malicious repository containing prompt-injection content and run
Claude Code against it -- this is a chained attack (prompt injection ->
sandbox-scoped tool misuse -> host-level persistence), not a
network-reachable exploit on its own.

Detection logic flags the specific, near-never-legitimate act at the
center of the chain: a `git worktree add` invocation whose target name is
literally `.git` -- ordinary worktree usage never names a worktree this
way, since it collides with git's own internal directory name, so this is
a high-precision signal rather than a heuristic on worktree usage in
general.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (Anthropic, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 2.1.163.
